scope: Owner-local certificate issuance only, after native HTTP acceptance; no TLS deployment or renewal activation

knownState.edgeCertbot: Absent before this phase; no install attempted

accountDiscovery.officialCommand: certbot show_account with explicit selected local storage ID, existing /etc/letsencrypt namespace, exact production server, isolated inspection logs/work, explicit empty hooks
accountDiscovery.warning: show_account uses the existing account internally to query the CA. It can create normal local logs/locks. It does not create an account when none exists.
accountDiscovery.requestedEmailSource: Only verified existing account/operator metadata; no invented email and no Google credentials

accountPreparation.mainPreferred: After reviewing the exact host-local seeding scope under the current task authorization, copy only the selected existing account's regr.json/meta.json/private_key.json within main to /etc/imonmeets/acme/main/accounts/acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory/<LOCAL_ID>. Use exclusive new root0700 directories/root-private files; never print key bytes. Copy no old live/archive/renewal/hooks and never share a writable symlink to the old account tree.
accountPreparation.mainValidation: Official show_account from the new main namespace must match the selected old account URL/thumbprint before certonly. The old meets-imon-world lineage and its renewal remain unchanged.
accountPreparation.edge: Create its own new account key locally only after separate account/contact/terms authorization. Never copy main account keys to edge.
accountPreparation.consent: No registration and no agreement flag are approved or executed by this plan. Existing-account consent is not a new-account registration decision.
accountPreparation.missingContact: show_account may return none. Do not fabricate ACME_EMAIL; choose a verified operator contact or explicitly reviewed no-email registration mode separately.
accountPreparation.accountIdMeaning: --account requires Certbot's local storage identifier, not the numeric ACME account URL identifier.

edgePackagePrerequisites.hostCandidatesAndDependencyDelta: Unknown until tool usage is available and the bounded read-only batch completes after fresh review.
edgePackagePrerequisites.laterInstallGate: Review exact complete dependency/version/size delta and official origins; require no upgrades/removals. Pin the accepted plan. Do not enable a new repository, run apt update, use snap/pip, or install webserver plugins automatically.
edgePackagePrerequisites.laterAutostartPlan: On EDGE only: inspect stock Certbot unit/timer/cron state; refuse unreviewed existing policy or unit overrides. Before apt, use an exclusively owned temporary policy-rc.d exit101 and persistent masks for stock certbot.service AND certbot.timer. Keep stock nginx.service masked. NEEDRESTART_MODE=l. No main timer/service/hook changes.
edgePackagePrerequisites.aptBound: Use the reviewed finite apt deadline with no forced dpkg kill; retain temporary policy if apt/children lifetime is uncertain; remove only the exact owned policy after confirmed process exit.
laterPostchecks: Existing native HTTP and WireGuard state preserved
Packaged cron's systemd skip condition inspected

requirements: Native HTTP proof passes for all five real names; correct challenge bytes from the correct owner-local webroot.
Fresh public DNS including any AAAA and CAA does not contradict the approved HTTP path.
Target /etc/imonmeets/acme/main and witness namespaces are new or explicitly reviewed; target certificate names have no conflicting lineage.
Inspect default /etc/letsencrypt/cli.ini and root XDG/default cli.ini keys without exposing values. Explicit --config does not exclude these defaults.
Refuse unreviewed inherited options. Keep explicit empty pre/post/deploy/renew hook arguments and --no-directory-hooks.
Both chosen namespace-local accounts exist and were independently validated; no implicit registration in certonly.
Resolve certificate names from reviewed TLS_CERT_NAME and EDGE_WITNESS_TLS_CERT_NAME; they must be distinct and satisfy the existing generator constraints.
isolationPreflight.directoryOwnership: Config, account, work and log directories root-owned/private. Existing public challenge roots must remain readable by the approved HTTP worker. Certbot2.9 webroot deliberately creates challenge files mode0644 under its own temporary umask022.

issueOnly.bound: --issuance-timeout90 limits issuance polling; additionally use a reviewed finite caller deadline with cleanup allowance. One attempt per role; inspect failure before any retry.
issueOnly.note: These commands use already prepared accounts. Certbot may write its own new lineage renewal metadata, but no timer or hook is activated.

required: Owner-local certificate/key public-key match checked without key export
Existing main meets-imon-world lineage and global renewal settings unchanged
No new listener or full TLS context activation

findings: Its issue argv already uses certonly/webroot and separate config/work/log directories.
Its generated certbot.ini unconditionally contains agree-tos=true and it requires complete renewal runtime contexts.
Do not generate fictional runtime contexts merely to issue certificates. The direct owner-local issue argv above requires no Node runtime.
Do not run stageInitial, reconcile, renew, renewal timers, or install managed TLS contexts during issuance-only.

sourceVerifiedCaveats: Certbot2.9 show_account checks for an existing local account before selecting/querying it; absence returns an error rather than register.
A local --account ID is resolved inside --config-dir; the same email or old ID alone does not transfer identity to an empty namespace.
Certbot2.9 and ConfigArgParse1.7 load default config files as well as an explicit --config file.
Certbot2.9 --dry-run switches to staging; when an accounts tree exists it may set terms acceptance and no-email registration flags automatically. It is not a read-only prerequisite.
Certbot2.9 regr.json stores body={} and cannot be relied upon as a saved email source.
editorialClarification: The full generator ran in synthetic tests; no production issuance was executed. Existing user authorization remains applicable; evaluate any future account/contact/terms action against that scope rather than requesting duplicate permission automatically.
